items.title: bh_hal_idle_eth.cpp:58 + qa_hal_idle_eth.cpp:58 — copy-paste-wrong-macro: idle-eth UNRESERVED derived from MEM_AERISC_MAP_END overlaps KERNEL_CONFIG by 2544 B
items.body:
Split out of #51225, combining **items 6 and 7** — they are the same copy-paste slip in two architectures and the parent asks for them to be fixed as one change.

Verified still present on current `main`: `bh_hal_idle_eth.cpp:56-58` and `qa_hal_idle_eth.cpp:56-58` are byte-identical in the relevant expression.

**On Blackhole and Quasar, the IDLE_ETH `UNRESERVED` base is derived from `MEM_AERISC_MAP_END` (the *active*-eth map end) while the IDLE_ETH `KERNEL_CONFIG` base is `MEM_IERISC_MAP_END`, so the idle-eth kernel-config ring buffer overlaps the start of the unreserved/allocatable L1 region by 2544 bytes on both arches.**

## The code

Both files, lines 56-58 — the base uses IERISC but the unreserved start uses AERISC:

```cpp
mem_map_bases[static_cast<std::size_t>(HalL1MemAddrType::KERNEL_CONFIG)] = MEM_IERISC_MAP_END;
mem_map_bases[static_cast<std::size_t>(HalL1MemAddrType::UNRESERVED)] =
    tt::align(MEM_AERISC_MAP_END + MEM_ERISC_KERNEL_CONFIG_SIZE, max_alignment);
```

The sibling that does it correctly is the Wormhole idle-eth map, `tt_metal/llrt/hal/tt-1xx/wormhole/wh_hal_idle_eth.cpp:57-59` — both derived from `MEM_IERISC_MAP_END`:

```cpp
mem_map_bases[static_cast<std::size_t>(HalL1MemAddrType::KERNEL_CONFIG)] = MEM_IERISC_MAP_END;
mem_map_bases[static_cast<std::size_t>(HalL1MemAddrType::UNRESERVED)] =
    ((MEM_IERISC_MAP_END + L1_KERNEL_CONFIG_SIZE - 1) | (max_alignment - 1)) + 1;
```

The active-eth files are self-consistent (`KERNEL_CONFIG = MEM_AERISC_MAP_END`, `UNRESERVED = align(MEM_AERISC_MAP_END + MEM_ERISC_KERNEL_CONFIG_SIZE, ...)`), which is where the AERISC expression was copied from.

## Numbers

Values obtained by preprocessing `tt_metal/hw/inc/internal/{tt-1xx/blackhole,tt-2xx/quasar}/dev_mem_map.h`; `MEM_ERISC_KERNEL_CONFIG_SIZE = 25600`, `max_alignment = max(DRAM_ALIGNMENT=64, L1_ALIGNMENT=16) = 64`:

| | `MEM_IERISC_MAP_END` | `MEM_AERISC_MAP_END` | KERNEL_CONFIG span | UNRESERVED (as written) | overlap | UNRESERVED (fixed) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blackhole | 64816 | 62256 | [64816, 90416) | 87872 | **2544 B** | 90432 |
| Quasar | 65520 | 62944 | [65520, 91120) | 88576 | **2544 B** | 91136 |

On both arches corruption begins once the ring reaches **offset 23056** within the 25600-byte kernel-config buffer.

The macros diverge because the idle map additionally reserves the routing table / routing paths / exit-node table (`MEM_ROUTING_TABLE_SIZE = 2576`): BH differs by 2560, Quasar by 2576.

## How it fails

Consequences are identical on both arches — silent data corruption or a hang, **not** a clean `TT_FATAL`:

- `tt_metal/impl/program/dispatch.cpp:2386-2400` (`initialize_worker_config_buf_mgr`) registers the idle-eth config ring buffer as `(base=KERNEL_CONFIG, size=get_dev_size(KERNEL_CONFIG))`. Once a program — or a sequence of programs cycling the ring — reaches offset ≥ 23056, dispatch writes RTAs/semaphores/kernel binaries on top of L1 already handed out from `UNRESERVED`.
- `tt_metal/impl/dispatch/dispatch_mem_map.cpp:59` places the ETH-dispatch command-queue structures at `l1_base = get_dev_addr(IDLE_ETH, UNRESERVED)`, i.e. 2544 bytes inside the still-live idle-eth kernel-config ring, so an eth-dispatch build can have its CQ state clobbered by a large idle-eth program.
- `tt_metal/impl/dispatch/kernel_config/relay_mux.cpp:33` takes the same `IDLE_ETH`/`UNRESERVED` address for a fabric relay mux on an eth core.

Nothing catches the overlap because `finalize_program_offsets` only checks against the (wrongly large) 25600 size. The invariant being violated is stated by the codebase itself at `dispatch.cpp:2390-2393`, where for `TENSIX` the ring-buffer size is *derived* as `worker_l1_unreserved_start - get_dev_addr(TENSIX, KERNEL_CONFIG)` — i.e. kernel config must end exactly at the unreserved start. The non-TENSIX branch trusts `get_dev_size(KERNEL_CONFIG)` instead.

## Origin

`git log -L 56,59` on `bh_hal_idle_eth.cpp` shows commit `248afccc12c` ("Use a single memory map for Blackhole ETH", #21582) replaced the `MEM_IERISC_MAP_END`-based expression with the `MEM_AERISC_MAP_END` one but left `KERNEL_CONFIG` on `MEM_IERISC_MAP_END`; the two macros have since diverged.

## Suggested fix

In **both** `bh_hal_idle_eth.cpp:57-58` and `qa_hal_idle_eth.cpp:57-58`, use the same map end the `KERNEL_CONFIG` entry uses, matching `wh_hal_idle_eth.cpp`:

```cpp
mem_map_bases[static_cast<std::size_t>(HalL1MemAddrType::UNRESERVED)] =
    tt::align(MEM_IERISC_MAP_END + MEM_ERISC_KERNEL_CONFIG_SIZE, max_alignment);
```

Additionally, to stop this class of drift recurring:

- Add a `static_assert`/`TT_FATAL` that `mem_map_bases[UNRESERVED] >= mem_map_bases[KERNEL_CONFIG] + mem_map_sizes[KERNEL_CONFIG]` for every core type.
- Fix the wrong macro in the corroborating slip in the same family: `bh_hal_active_eth.cpp:81` and `qa_hal_active_eth.cpp:46` both `static_assert(MEM_IERISC_MAP_END % L1_ALIGNMENT == 0)` — a constant neither active-eth file uses — instead of `MEM_AERISC_MAP_END`.

items.title: [ttnn/ccl] reduce_to_root: wrong intermediate tensor spec and a 2-page CB overflow
items.body:
These are statically audited bugs. The issues have enough detail that you can point claude and ask it to fix them. There is a small chance of false positives.

---

Two high-severity defects in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/ccl/reduce_to_root/`, one host-side and one device-side.

**Line references are against `02246470f99`, and every file below was re-checked as byte-identical on `main` @ `007e45f8bfe`, so the line numbers are valid as of filing. If lines have since moved, the quoted code in each entry is the reliable anchor.**

Each item is self-contained — location, triggering configuration, evidence, and a suggested fix — and is independently fixable. Please tick items off as they land rather than closing the issue on the first fix.

CODEOWNERS: @tenstorrent/metalium-developers-ops-data-movement

The two are independent, but both are in the same op so a single pass over `reduce_to_root` covers them. Item 1 is host-side (the intermediate tensor spec is one shard wide instead of the whole per-device tensor, and reuses the wrong shard shape); item 2 is a device-side CB overflow that overruns `c_18` by 2 pages — 1 KB with the shipped config — corrupting whatever L1 follows.

Prior art in the same op, neither overlapping these: #50308 (closed) fixed a deferred `noc_async_read_barrier` in `root_receive_reader_kernel.cpp`, and #48586 discusses the op in passing. Different files, different defects.

| # | Sev | Location | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | H | [`ccl/reduce_to_root/device/reduce_to_root_op.cpp:99`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/007e45f8bfe/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/ccl/reduce_to_root/device/reduce_to_root_op.cpp#L99) | The auto-computed intermediate tensor spec is one shard wide (shard_w + 2*s_shard_w) instead of the whole per-device tensor, and it reuses the l tensor's layout (... |
| 2 | H | [`ccl/reduce_to_root/device/reduce_to_root_program.cpp:358`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/007e45f8bfe/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/ccl/reduce_to_root/device/reduce_to_root_program.cpp#L358) | CB c_18 (packet_cb_id_2, used by root2_writer_kernel) is allocated only packet_size_bytes, but the writer fills it with packet_size_bytes + 2*aligned_page_size_by... |

---

### 1. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/ccl/reduce_to_root/device/reduce_to_root_op.cpp:99` — wrong-shape/units

**The auto-computed intermediate tensor spec is one shard wide (shard_w + 2*s_shard_w) instead of the whole per-device tensor, and it reuses the l tensor's layout (shard shape [8,128]) instead of a [8,192] shard, so each core's intermediate allocation is smaller than the packet the kernels write into it.**

**How it fails.** Call ttnn.reduce_to_root without intermediate_tensor (exactly what tests/ttnn/docs_examples/test_ccl_examples.py::test_reduce_to_root does): l is [8, 128*8] width-sharded [8,128] over 8 cores, s/m [8, 32*8] sharded [8,32]. compute_output_specs builds intermediate_shape = Shape{8, 128 + 2*32} = [8,192] and TensorSpec(intermediate_shape, l.tensor_layout()), i.e. shard spec still [8,128]. That tensor is only 6 pages wide => 2 shards distributed round-robin over the 8-core grid, so each L1 bank reserves 1 shard = 4 pages = 2048 B. Every one of the 8 shard cores then has 3072 B (packet_size_bytes + 2*aligned_page = 2048+1024) written to intermediate_tensor.buffer()->address() by the fabric fused write (sender_writer / root2_writer) and read back with the same size by the receive readers, overrunning the 2048 B allocation by 1 KB per core and silently corrupting adjacent L1.

**Evidence.** reduce_to_root_op.cpp lines 95-101: `uint32_t shape_0 = final_output_spec[0].memory_config().shard_spec()->shape[0]; uint32_t shape_1 = final_output_spec[0].memory_config().shard_spec()->shape[1] + (2 * final_output_spec[1].memory_config().shard_spec()->shape[1]); Shape intermediate_shape = Shape{shape_0, shape_1}; TensorSpec intermediate_spec(intermediate_shape, final_output_spec[0].tensor_layout());` -- shape built from SHARD dims (no num_cores factor) while the layout carries the l tensor's shard spec. The intended spec is spelled out by the caller that supplies its own intermediate in tests/.../nightly/test_reduce_to_root_trace.py: `intermediate_shapes = [[8, 192 * num_cores]]` with `shard_spec_int_l = ttnn.ShardSpec(shard_grid, [8, 192], ...)`. Kernel-side size: root_receive_reader_kernel.cpp l.95 `new_packet_size_bytes = packet_size_bytes + 2 * align(page_size_bytes, alignment)` read from `intermediate_base_addr`, and sender_writer_kernel.cpp l.53 writes the same size to the remote intermediate address.

**Suggested fix.** Build the intermediate spec for the full per-device tensor and give it its own shard spec: shape {shard_h, (shard_w + 2*s_shard_w) * num_shard_cores} with a MemoryConfig whose shard shape is {shard_h, shard_w + 2*s_shard_w} on the same grid (mirror what the trace test constructs), instead of reusing final_output_spec[0].tensor_layout().

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-ops-data-movement`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 2. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/ccl/reduce_to_root/device/reduce_to_root_program.cpp:358` — buffer-overflow

**CB c_18 (packet_cb_id_2, used by root2_writer_kernel) is allocated only packet_size_bytes, but the writer fills it with packet_size_bytes + 2*aligned_page_size_bytes, writing 2 pages (1 KB with the shipped config) past the end of the circular buffer.**

**How it fails.** 4-device line, root at (1,0) (the shipped test config): l shard [8,128], tile (8,32), bf16 => input_page_size_bytes=512, input_num_tiles=4, packet_size_bytes=2048. cb_packet_config_2 total size = 2048 B (1 page). root2_writer_kernel computes new_payload_size_bytes = payload_size_bytes + 2*aligned_page_size_bytes = 2048 + 1024 = 3072 and tt_memmoves the s page to packet_base_addr+2048 and the m page to packet_base_addr+2560, i.e. 1024 bytes beyond the CB, then DMAs 3072 bytes from that base over fabric. The 1 KB tail lands in whatever CB the L1 allocator placed after c_18 (for the root2 device the next CB created is c_11 / compute_out_cb_l), silently corrupting another kernel's L1 region; any change in dtype/tile/shard size makes the clobbered region live.

**Evidence.** Program factory: `constexpr auto packet_cb_id_2 = tt::CBIndex::c_18; CircularBufferConfig cb_packet_config_2 = CircularBufferConfig(packet_size_bytes, {{packet_cb_id_2, input_dataformat}}).set_page_size(packet_cb_id_2, packet_size_bytes);` (lines 356-360) versus the sibling sized correctly for exactly the same packet layout: `auto total_pkt_size = packet_size_bytes + 1024; ... CircularBufferConfig(2 * total_pkt_size, {{packet_cb_id, input_dataformat}}).set_page_size(packet_cb_id, total_pkt_size)` (lines 278-283). Consumer root2_writer_kernel.cpp: `const uint32_t new_payload_size_bytes = payload_size_bytes + 2 * aligned_page_size_bytes;` (l.108) with `packet_base_addr = get_write_ptr(packet_cb_id)` (l.112), writes at `packet_base_addr + payload_size_bytes` (l.127) and `+ payload_size_bytes + aligned_page_size_bytes` (l.134), then `send_payload_without_header_non_blocking_from_address(packet_base_addr, new_payload_size_bytes)` (l.149). writer_ct_args for root2 pass packet_cb_id_2 as the packet CB and packet_size_bytes as payload_size_bytes (lines 584-594).

**Suggested fix.** Size c_18 like c_7: `CircularBufferConfig(total_pkt_size, {{packet_cb_id_2, input_dataformat}}).set_page_size(packet_cb_id_2, total_pkt_size)` (and prefer `packet_size_bytes + 2 * aligned_input_page_size_bytes` over the hard-coded +1024 in total_pkt_size, which only happens to be right for bf16 8x32 tiles).

items.title: [ttnn/embedding] 4 high-severity defects: index-CB overflow, dead traversal branch, wrong face offset, floor-vs-ceil tiles
items.body:
These are statically audited bugs. The issues have enough detail that you can point claude and ask it to fix them. There is a small chance of false positives.

---

Four high-severity defects in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/embedding/` (3) and `embedding_backward/` (1) — the forward/backward pair of the same op.

**Line references are against `02246470f99`, and every file below was re-checked as byte-identical on `main` @ `007e45f8bfe`, so the line numbers are valid as of filing. If lines have since moved, the quoted code in each entry is the reliable anchor.**

Each item is self-contained — location, triggering configuration, evidence, and a suggested fix — and is independently fixable. Please tick items off as they land rather than closing the issue on the first fix.

CODEOWNERS: @tenstorrent/metalium-developers-ops-data-movement @TT-BrianLiu

---

### 1. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/embedding/device/embeddings_tilized_indices_program_factory.cpp:98` — device-kernel-cb-overflow

**Index scratch CB c_1 is sized FACE_HEIGHT*index_page_size (512B) but the reader NOC-reads one full aligned input page (2048B bf16 / 4096B uint32 tile) into it, overrunning the CB.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.embedding with TILE_LAYOUT uint32 indices (selects EmbeddingsTilizedIndicesProgramFactory) - e.g. ids of shape (1,2048) uint32 TILE. Each core's reader does noc.async_read(input, input_l1_addr, input.get_aligned_page_size()=4096B) into a 512B CB, writing 3584B past the end of cb_id_in1 into whatever L1 follows it. Watcher's NOC sanitizer halts on the out-of-bounds write; without watcher it silently corrupts neighbouring L1.

**Evidence.** Factory: `uint32_t index_page_size = round_up_to_mul32(input_element_size_bytes);` then `.total_size = FACE_HEIGHT * index_page_size` and `.page_size = FACE_HEIGHT * index_page_size` (16*32 = 512B). Kernel embedding_ind_tilized.cpp:51,71: `const uint32_t input_page_size = input.get_aligned_page_size();` ... `noc.async_read(input, CoreLocalMem<uint32_t>(input_l1_addr), input_page_size, {.page_id = curr_tile}, {});` - a whole 32x32 tile page. The kernel also indexes `input_l1_ptr[token_idx + offset]` with offset up to 1008 (face 3, row 15), so it requires a full tile of storage. Sibling factories size this CB to exactly what they read: embeddings_rm_program_factory.cpp:140-148 (block_height*index_page_size vs a block_height*elem_size read) and embeddings_fused_program_factory.cpp:146-154 (TILE_HEIGHT*elem_size vs an input_block_size_bytes read).

**Suggested fix.** Size cb_id_in1 to at least one full aligned input page: `std::max<uint32_t>(FACE_HEIGHT * index_page_size, a.buffer()->aligned_page_size())` for both total_size and page_size.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-ops-data-movement @TT-BrianLiu`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 2. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/embedding/device/kernels/dataflow/embedding_ind_tilized.cpp:84` — always-false-condition

**`if (offset == tile_height * tile_height)` (1024) can never be true - offset maxes out at 1008 - so the 'advance to the next tile row' path is dead and the traversal wraps back into the current tile.**

**How it fails.** Same TILE-index (96,32) case: core 21 covers tokens 1008..1055 = tile rows 31 and 32. At the end of row 31, offset = 768 + 15*16 = 1008 and face = 3, so `offset == 1024` is false; the else branch does `curr_tile -= (tiles_per_row-1)` and `offset -= 240` -> 768 = face 3 row 0 of the same tile, instead of curr_tile + tiles_per_row with offset 0. All remaining tokens on that core index the wrong tile and faces.

**Evidence.** `offset` is always face_base in {0,256,512,768} plus row_in_face*16 in {0..240}, max 1008; assignments are only `offset = 0`, `+= face_hw`, `-= face_hw`, `+= face_size`, `-= face_size*(face_size-1)`, so the comparison to 1024 is dead. The ONLY_ONE_FACE_COLUMN branch uses the correct last-row test `last_column_face_2 = offset - (face_hw*3 - face_size); if (last_column_face_2 < face_size) { offset = 0; curr_tile++; }`, and the host formula (embeddings_tilized_indices_program_factory.cpp:200-204) gives offset 0, curr_tile = (32/32)*tiles_per_row for row 32.

**Suggested fix.** Test `offset == tile_height * tile_height - face_size` (1008) and advance `curr_tile += tiles_per_row` (not `curr_tile++`, correct only when tiles_per_row == 1) with offset = 0, accounting for the rewind done in the sibling branch.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-ops-data-movement @TT-BrianLiu`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 3. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/embedding/device/kernels/dataflow/embedding_ind_tilized.cpp:114` — wrong-index-math

**End-of-row advance `offset -= face_size*(face_size-1)` does not handle the last row of a face row-half: after tile row 15 it lands on face 1 row 0 (offset 256) instead of face 2 row 0 (offset 512), so the wrong index tokens are read.**

**How it fails.** TILE_LAYOUT uint32 index tensor of shape (96,32) on an 8x8 grid: split_work_to_cores_aligned gives units_per_core = 48 tokens, so core 10 covers tokens 480..527 = tile rows 15 and 16. After finishing row 15 (offset = 496 = face1 row15, face = 1) the code does `offset -= face_size*(face_size-1)` -> 256 = face 1 row 0; row 16 must come from face 2 (offset 512). That core's last 16 output rows are the embeddings of the wrong tokens.

**Evidence.** Kernel: `} else { offset -= face_size * (face_size - 1); }` inside the `col_offset == row_length` branch. The host computes the same quantity correctly for a core's starting row: embeddings_tilized_indices_program_factory.cpp:200 `uint32_t r_f_offset = (((row % TILE_HEIGHT) / FACE_HEIGHT) * 2 * FACE_HW) + ((row % FACE_HEIGHT) * FACE_HEIGHT);` -> 512 for row 16, while the kernel's incremental update yields 256. The ONLY_ONE_FACE_COLUMN variant of the same transition (lines 95-100) does handle it (`if (last_column_face_0 < face_size) offset += face_hw;`), showing the general path is missing the face-half jump.

**Suggested fix.** In the odd-face end-of-row case, detect row-in-face == 15 and jump to the next face row-half (offset += 2*FACE_HW - face_size*(face_size-1)) instead of unconditionally subtracting 240; or recompute offset from the running (row,col) with the host's formula.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-ops-data-movement @TT-BrianLiu`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 4. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/embedding_backward/device/embedding_backward_program_descriptor.cpp:61` — truncating-integer-division

**num_embeddings_tiles uses floor division (num_embeddings / TILE_HEIGHT) while the output tensor is allocated with ceil(num_embeddings/32) tile rows, so when the vocabulary size is not a multiple of 32 the last (partial) tile row of the gradient output is never zero-initialised and never accumulated into - it is returned to the caller as uninitialised garbage.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.embedding_bw with a weight tensor whose vocab size is not a multiple of 32 (e.g. GPT-2 50257, BERT 30522, T5 32100). For num_embeddings=50257: compute_output_specs builds ttnn::Shape({1,1,50257,dim}) in TILE layout -> the buffer has ceil(50257/32)=1571 tile rows. The descriptor passes num_embeddings_tiles = 50257/32 = 1570 as reader compile-time arg 3, so reader_embedding_backward.cpp's zero-fill loop `for (i = 0; i < num_embeddings; ++i)` (line 141) writes zeros to only tile rows 0..1569. Output logical rows 50240..50256 are never written -> caller reads stale buffer contents. Worse, any index in [50240, 50257) produces chunk_idx = idx>>5 = 1570, and the accumulate path at line 207 (`out_tile_idx = chunk_idx * tiles_per_hidden + hidden_offset`) reads that never-zeroed tile into cb_out_intermed, adds the gradient to garbage, and writes it back, so those tokens' gradients are also wrong.

**Evidence.** embedding_backward_program_descriptor.cpp:61 `uint32_t num_embeddings_tiles = operation_attributes.num_embeddings / TILE_HEIGHT;` (floor), passed at line 155 as reader compile-time arg 3. reader_embedding_backward.cpp:102 `constexpr uint32_t num_embeddings = get_compile_time_arg_val(3);` and 141 `for (uint32_t i = 0; i < num_embeddings; ++i)` is the ONLY code that initialises the output buffer. embedding_backward_device_operation.cpp:75 allocates `ttnn::Shape({1, 1, operation_attributes.num_embeddings, embedding_dim})` in TILE layout, i.e. ceil(n/32) tile rows. num_embeddings comes from the user's logical vocab size: embedding_backward.cpp:23 `auto num_embeddings = weight_tensor_arg.logical_shape()[-2];`. validate_on_program_cache_miss (embedding_backward_device_operation.cpp:22-67) enforces `index_tensor_shape[-1] % TILE_WIDTH == 0` and `grad_tensor_shape[-1] % TILE_WIDTH == 0` but has NO `num_embeddings % TILE_HEIGHT == 0` guard. Sibling that does it correctly: ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/embedding/device/embeddings_tilized_indices_program_factory.cpp:189 `uint32_t tiles_per_tile_row = (num_cols + TILE_HEIGHT - 1) / TILE_HEIGHT;` (ceil-div), and the forward op ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/embedding/device/embedding_device_operation.cpp:50 explicitly TT_FATALs on `% TILE_HEIGHT == 0`. Every existing test uses a multiple of 32 (tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/data_movement/test_backward_embedding.py: 96, 320, 3200; the sweep generates vocab in steps of 32 from 32), so the case is untested.

**Suggested fix.** Use ceil division: `uint32_t num_embeddings_tiles = tt::div_up(operation_attributes.num_embeddings, TILE_HEIGHT);` so the whole padded output (including the final partial tile row) is zeroed and accumulated. The mask path already handles a partial tile correctly (generate_mask only marks rows whose index falls in [chunk_id*32, chunk_id*32+32)). Alternatively, if only multiples of 32 are intended to be supported, add `TT_FATAL(num_embeddings % TILE_HEIGHT == 0, ...)` to validate_on_program_cache_miss, mirroring the forward embedding op.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-ops-data-movement @TT-BrianLiu`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

items.title: [ttnn/normalization] 7 high-severity defects: missing CB reserve, host/kernel arg mismatch, wrong index
items.body:
These are statically audited bugs. The issues have enough detail that you can point claude and ask it to fix them. There is a small chance of false positives.

---

Seven high-severity defects in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/` that do **not** hang the op — they corrupt a CB, read uninitialized args, or silently return the wrong numbers. (The six deadlocks in this area are filed separately.)

**Line references are against `02246470f99`, and every file below was re-checked as byte-identical on `main` @ `007e45f8bfe`, so the line numbers are valid as of filing. If lines have since moved, the quoted code in each entry is the reliable anchor.**

Each item is self-contained — location, triggering configuration, evidence, and a suggested fix — and is independently fixable. Please tick items off as they land rather than closing the issue on the first fix.

CODEOWNERS: @tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce

Three groups:

- **Item 1** writes a CB without reserving space, so it can overwrite tiles the consumer has not popped yet.
- **Items 2-4: host and kernel disagree.** Items 3 and 4 are in the same file and each shifts every subsequent kernel arg by one word, so fix them together — one omits a compile-time arg the reader still reads, the other still passes a runtime arg that was removed. Item 2 is the CB-existence variant: the kernel compiles in a block whose args and CB the host only supplies on a different path.
- **Items 5-7: wrong index or truncated type.** In bounds and well-formed, but addressing the wrong tile or truncating a count by its declared type.

### 1. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/layernorm_distributed/device/kernels/compute/layernorm_pre_allgather_welford.cpp:299` — cb-credit-imbalance

**The compute kernel packs and pushes 2 tiles into the output CB c_14 every row iteration but never calls cb_out.reserve_back(2), so the producer never waits for the writer to free space.**

**How it fails.** NCHt greater than (c_14 capacity / 2) row iterations on any core (c_14 total size is block_size*2 tiles and block_size = gcd(Wt, 4|8) can be 1, i.e. a 2-tile CB). Once the pack side wraps the CB, `pack_tile(dst0, cb_out_idx)` overwrites tiles the writer has not yet DMA'd out (the writer only does wait_front(1)/pop_front(1) per tile), so the stats output gets garbled rows whenever the DRAM write side stalls. No back-pressure at all -> timing-dependent corruption.

**Evidence.** Lines 289-300: `tile_regs_acquire(); cb_scratch.wait_front(2); transpose_tile(...); transpose_tile(...); cb_scratch.pop_front(2); tile_regs_commit(); tile_regs_wait(); pack_tile(dst0, cb_out_idx); pack_tile(dst1, cb_out_idx); cb_out.push_back(2); tile_regs_release();` — grep of `cb_out.` over the file returns only line 299; there is no reserve_back anywhere. The same kernel does it correctly for its scratch CB (215/220 and 277/282), and the non-Welford sibling writes c_14 through compute_kernel_lib::reduce which always pairs `output_dfb.reserve_back(...)` with `output_dfb.push_back(...)` (reduce_helpers_compute.inl:385/456, 470/565). CircularBuffer::push_back (tt_metal/hw/inc/api/dataflow/circular_buffer.h:43) only calls llk_push_tiles and does not wait for free pages.

**Suggested fix.** Add `cb_out.reserve_back(2);` before the `tile_regs_wait()` / pack_tile pair at line 296, matching the cb_scratch handling in the same loop.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

### 2. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/layernorm/device/kernels/dataflow/writer_unary_sharded_ln.cpp:41` — guard-mismatch-uninitialized-read

**The reshard write-back block is compiled in whenever skip_write_back is false, but the host only pushes the write-back runtime args (and only creates CB c_17) when is_post_all_gather is true; a non-distributed sharded layernorm whose output shard spec differs from the input's therefore reads runtime args that were never written and issues NOC writes with garbage size/coordinates.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.layer_norm(sharded_input, program_config=LayerNormShardedMultiCoreProgramConfig{...}, memory_config=<sharded, same grid+shape but ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR>). Validation passes (only buffer_type and memory_layout are checked against the input, not the shard spec). layernorm_op_multi_core_sharded.cpp:98 computes skip_write_back = (output.shard_spec() == a.shard_spec()) = false, and is_post_all_gather = false. KernelDefines::build (sharded_layernorm_factory_helpers.cpp:512) only emits SKIP_WRITE_BACK when skip_write_back, so the kernel keeps the write-back block. build_write_back_args (same file:1557) returns {} because !is_post_all_gather, so build_writer_args pushes exactly 6 runtime args (indices 0..5). The kernel then executes get_arg_val<uint32_t>(6)/(7) and get_arg_addr(8), reading L1 past the end of this kernel's runtime-arg region, and passes that garbage as num_segments_to_write_back / storage_core_start_offset / segment_args into write_resharded_data(), which issues noc.async_write() unicasts of arbitrary length to arbitrary {noc_x, noc_y}. CB c_17 (cb_out_resharded), whose named CT arg is always supplied (helpers:850) but whose descriptor is only created under `is_post_all_gather && !skip_write_back` (helpers:1324), is also read via get_write_ptr() while unconfigured.

**Evidence.** writer_unary_sharded_ln.cpp:40-44 `#ifndef SKIP_WRITE_BACK / const uint32_t num_segments_to_write_back = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(6); ... segment_args = (tt_l1_ptr uint32_t*)(get_arg_addr(8)); #endif` and :116-127 the matching call to write_resharded_data(). Host side: sharded_layernorm_factory_helpers.cpp:512 `if (skip_write_back) { defines.writer.emplace_back("SKIP_WRITE_BACK", "1"); }` -- gated on skip_write_back ONLY; :1554-1559 `build_write_back_args(...) { if (!ctx.is_post_all_gather) { return args; } ...}` -- args produced ONLY when is_post_all_gather; :1594-1612 build_writer_args appends those (empty) args after its 6 fixed args; :1324 `if (cb_config.is_post_all_gather && !cb_config.skip_write_back)` -- c_17 created ONLY when is_post_all_gather. The two conditions disagree exactly on the case !is_post_all_gather && !skip_write_back. The identical defect is present in the sibling writer writer_unary_sharded_ln_rm_gb.cpp:43-47 and :153-164.

**Suggested fix.** Make the define match the host-side arg/CB condition, e.g. in layernorm_op_multi_core_sharded.cpp compute `bool skip_write_back = !is_post_all_gather || (output.shard_spec().value() == a.shard_spec().value());` (or emit SKIP_WRITE_BACK when `skip_write_back || !is_post_all_gather`). Alternatively add a TT_FATAL rejecting a non-distributed sharded layernorm whose output shard spec differs from the input's.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 3. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/layernorm_distributed/device/layernorm_post_all_gather_welford_program_factory.cpp:284` — kernel-arg-layout-mismatch

**Welford post-all-gather factory omits the `reduce_factor` compile-time arg that the shared reader kernel reads at index 8, so every TensorAccessorArgs offset in the reader is shifted by one word.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.layer_norm_post_all_gather(..., program_config=LayerNormDefaultProgramConfig(use_welford=True)) on any shape. The reader kernel builds `src_args = TensorAccessorArgs<9>()` but this factory only pushes 8 compile-time args (indices 0..7) before appending the input accessor args, which therefore start at index 8. The reader consumes CTA[8] (the src accessor's config word) as `reduce_factor` and then parses the src accessor starting one word late; stats/gamma/beta accessors are all shifted with it. Result: input/stats/gamma/beta DRAM addressing is computed from a misaligned accessor descriptor -> garbage reads (or a compile-time failure inside calculate_and_prepare_reduce_scaler if the borrowed word is 0).

**Evidence.** reader_unary_interleaved_ln_rm_gb_post_allgather.cpp:91-97 declares `cb_length = get_compile_time_arg_val(6); Wt = get_compile_time_arg_val(7); reduce_factor = get_compile_time_arg_val(8); src_args = TensorAccessorArgs<9>(); stats_args = TensorAccessorArgs<src_args.next...>(); ...`. The sibling non-Welford factory that drives the SAME reader source pushes 9 scalars: layernorm_post_all_gather_program_factory.cpp:243-247 `push_back(cb_length); push_back(tiles_per_core_y); const uint32_t reduce_factor = logical_W * num_devices; reader_compile_time_args.push_back(reduce_factor);` before appending accessors at 249. This factory (lines 254-257 `{block_size, stats_tiles_cols}` plus 279-284 gamma_stick_size, beta_stick_size, gamma_is_row_major, beta_is_row_major, cb_length, Wt) pushes only 8 and appends accessors at 286. Confirmed drift: commit 7fb82fd003d added the reduce_factor CTA to the reader and updated only the non-Welford factory (its diff of the Welford factory changed nothing but the c_5 CB format).

**Suggested fix.** Push the reduce factor before the accessor args, mirroring the non-Welford factory: `reader_compile_time_args.push_back(logical_W * num_devices);` immediately after `push_back(Wt)` on line 284.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 4. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/layernorm_distributed/device/layernorm_post_all_gather_welford_program_factory.cpp:353` — kernel-arg-layout-mismatch

**Welford post-all-gather factory still passes the removed `packed_winv_value` scaler runtime arg at index 5, shifting eps, gamma, beta, stats and y_offset by one slot relative to what the reader kernel reads.**

**How it fails.** Any Welford post-all-gather launch: the reader reads `eps = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(5)` and gets the packed bf16 1/W scaler; `gamma_addr = arg(6)` gets the epsilon bit pattern; `beta_addr = arg(7)` gets the gamma buffer address; `stats_addr = arg(8)` gets the beta address; `y_offset = arg(9)` gets the stats buffer address (a huge value used as a gamma/beta tile index). The kernel then DMAs from bogus DRAM addresses with a bogus epsilon -> wrong results or out-of-range reads.

**Evidence.** reader_unary_interleaved_ln_rm_gb_post_allgather.cpp:65-68 and 115: `gamma_addr = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(6); beta_addr = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(7); stats_addr = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(8); y_offset = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(9); ... const uint32_t eps = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(5);`. The sibling non-Welford factory emits exactly 10 runtime args with no scaler (layernorm_post_all_gather_program_factory.cpp:349-360), whereas this factory emits 11 (lines 346-358 and 382-394: `{a.buffer(), rows, Wt, tile_offset, stats_offset, packed_winv_value, eps, gamma_buffer, beta_buffer, stats.buffer(), y_offset}`), matching the pre-refactor reader that had `scaler = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(5)` / `eps = get_arg_val<uint32_t>(6)` (removed in commit 7fb82fd003d).

**Suggested fix.** Drop `packed_winv_value` (and the now-dead winv / bfloat16 / pack_two_bfloat16_into_uint32 helpers) from both runtime-arg lists so the layout matches the reader: {input, rows, Wt, tile_offset, stats_offset, eps, gamma, beta, stats, y_offset}.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 5. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/layernorm_distributed/device/kernels/compute/chain_llk.hpp:117` — wrong-index-math

**In the trailing partial pass, `wt` (the count of tiles already consumed in this chunk) is computed as register_loops * cb_leftovers instead of register_loops * DEST_capacity, so the persistent-CB_B tile index (gamma/beta) is wrong whenever Wt is > 4 and not a multiple of 4.**

**How it fails.** Distributed post-allgather LayerNorm/RMSNorm with gamma and/or beta and a per-core width Wt that is > 4 and not a multiple of 4 (e.g. W=192 -> Wt=6, W=320 -> Wt=10). The factory sets cb_length == tiles_per_core_y == Wt (layernorm_post_all_gather_program_factory.cpp:189/283 and ..._welford_program_factory.cpp:128), so the kernel takes pop_gamma_beta == 0xDDDD (layernorm_post_allgather.cpp:72). unroll_llk<6> then runs unroll_inner_loop<4>(0) (wt=0, tiles 0..3, gamma 0..3) followed by unroll_inner_loop<2>(1), where wt = 1*2 = 2 instead of 1*4 = 4. The last two output tiles are multiplied by gamma tiles 2,3 and added to beta tiles 2,3 instead of 4,5 -> silently wrong numerics (no hang, no assert). Existing tests never expose it: the CI shapes use W=8192 (Wt=256, %4==0) and the non-tile-aligned regression test uses input_w 17/34/63 (Wt=1 or 2, so cb_iterations==0 and wt==0 is accidentally correct).

**Evidence.** unroll_llk() (line 82-103) computes `constexpr uint32_t num_dst_regs = (is_fp_32 ? 4 : 8); constexpr uint32_t cb_iterations = cb_length / num_dst_regs; constexpr uint32_t cb_leftovers = cb_length % num_dst_regs;` then `for (i...) unroll_inner_loop<num_dst_regs>(i); unroll_inner_loop<cb_leftovers, cur_llk_type>(cb_iterations);`. Inside unroll_inner_loop the template parameter is *named* num_dst_regs but is bound to cb_leftovers on the trailing call, and line 117 does `uint32_t wt = register_loops * num_dst_regs;`. wt is then used as an absolute index into the never-popped CB_B: line 126 `cb_b.wait_front(num_dst_regs + (wt));` and line 134 `cb_b_index_policy<cur_llk_type>(j, wt)` -> line 57 `return wt + j;`. For the full passes register_loops*num_dst_regs is correct (i*4); for the trailing pass it must still be cb_iterations*4, not cb_iterations*cb_leftovers. CB_A is unaffected because it is popped each pass (lines 141-144), which is why only the 0xDDDD (persistent gamma/beta) path is corrupted. The reader confirms gamma/beta are persistent, pushed exactly once and never popped when Wt == cb_length: reader_unary_interleaved_ln_rm_gb_post_allgather.cpp:161 `if (ncht == 0 or cb_iterations != 1)`.

**Suggested fix.** Pass the already-consumed tile count explicitly instead of deriving it from the (possibly partial) block size, e.g. change unroll_inner_loop's signature to take `uint32_t tiles_done` and call `unroll_inner_loop<num_dst_regs>(i * num_dst_regs)` / `unroll_inner_loop<cb_leftovers>(cb_iterations * num_dst_regs)`, using `wt = tiles_done` directly.

### 6. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/softmax/device/kernels/attention/dataflow/reader_unary_interleaved_sm_large_tensor.cpp:133` — wrong-index

**Large-tensor softmax reader never advances the causal-mask page id from one tile-row to the next: every row inside a batch re-reads the same Wt mask tiles, so all rows get row-0's causal mask.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.scale_mask_softmax(..., is_causal_mask=True) on an interleaved tensor big enough that softmax_program_factory_attention_optimized.cpp:130 selects use_large_kernel (e.g. Wt >= ~300, mask present). With Ht = 8 tile-rows per batch, all 8 rows are masked with the SAME Wt mask tiles (the ones at start_mask_id) instead of rows 0..7 of the causal mask, so the attention output is numerically wrong for every row except the core's first one — silently, with no hang or assert.

**Evidence.** In the ncht loop the mask page cursor is reset every pass to a base that only moves at batch boundaries:
  line 94:  `mask_index = mask_id_offset;`   (executed at the top of EVERY cur_pass)
  lines 127-137 (end of each ncht = each tile-row):
    `++ht; ++mask_ht;
     if (ht == Ht) { ht = 0; mask_ht = 0; mask_id_offset += num_tiles_causal_mask; }
     else if (mask_ht == Wt) { mask_ht = 0; mask_id = mask_id_offset; }`
There is no `mask_id_offset += Wt` for the non-batch-boundary case, so mask_id_offset is constant across the Ht rows of a batch. The only per-row update writes to `mask_id`, which is dead after line 85 (`mask_index = mask_id`) — it is never read again, proving the bookkeeping was dropped. `mask_offset` (arg 12, read at line 26) is likewise never used, while the sibling reader uses it.
The correct sibling, reader_unary_interleaved_sm.cpp (same op, small-tensor path), gets the per-row advance for free because it never resets its cursor: `mask_id` is incremented inside the read loop (line 109 `++mask_id;`) and simply keeps running across rows, giving +Wt per row; only the batch base is bumped by num_tiles_causal_mask (line 119). The non-causal branch of the large reader also correctly advances its base once per batch (`mask_id_offset = mask_index;` line 144) — only the causal branch forgets the per-row step.
num_tiles_causal_mask is mask_Ht*mask_Wt (softmax_program_factory_attention_optimized.cpp:177-179), i.e. a whole-batch stride, confirming Wt is the intended per-row stride.

**Suggested fix.** In the CAUSAL_MASK epilogue, advance the per-row base: `mask_id_offset += Wt;` on the non-batch-boundary path (and set `mask_id_offset` back to the batch base + num_tiles_causal_mask when ht wraps), i.e. mirror reader_unary_interleaved_sm.cpp by keeping a running cursor instead of resetting `mask_index = mask_id_offset` to a base that never moves. Drop the dead `mask_id`/`mask_offset` locals or wire `mask_offset` into the wrap target as the small reader does.

### 7. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/normalization/groupnorm/device/groupnorm_sharded_program_factory.cpp:226` — type-truncation

**block_wt_last is declared `bool`, truncating the computed tile-count ceil(per_core_Nt / num_groups_per_core) to 1; the compute kernel consumes it as a tile width, so the last group's narrower block width is silently lost.**

**How it fails.** Sharded group_norm with a group size that is neither tile-aligned nor sub-tile, e.g. C = W = 800 (per_core_Nt = 25 tiles), num_groups = 16 -> num_datum_row_per_group = 50, height-sharded with per_core_N = 800 (num_groups_per_core = 16). find_max_tile_span(800,50) returns block_wt = 3 (a group starting at datum offset 30 straddles 3 tiles), while the last group (datums 750..799) spans only tiles 23..24, i.e. 2 tiles. The intended block_wt_last = (25 + 16 - 1)/16 = 2, but `bool` truncates it to 1. In groupnorm_sharded_v2.cpp:447 the test `index_g_offset == (per_core_N - block_w_last)` becomes `23 == 25 - 1` which is false, so block_w_curr falls back to block_w = 3 for the last group. The final copy/add loop at lines 452-479 then runs w = 0,1,2 and packs to `index = w + index_h_offset` with index_h_offset starting at index_b_offset + 23 and stepping by per_core_N per row: it writes tile column 25 of a 25-tile row, i.e. one tile past the end of every output row (and past the end of cb_out for the last row of the last batch), corrupting the output. The index_block_w / copy_or_add / group_reset_index bookkeeping in the same loop also advances one extra step, so the copy-vs-add decision for the group desynchronizes.

**Evidence.** Declaration: `bool block_wt_last = (per_core_Nt + num_groups_per_core - 1) / num_groups_per_core;` (line 226). The right-hand side is an integer ceil-division producing a tile count; assigning it to `bool` collapses every non-zero result to 1. The value is logged as a width (`log_debug(tt::LogOp, "block_wt_last: {}", block_wt_last);`, line 244) and shipped verbatim as compile-time arg 20 to both compute kernels (lines 670 and 704). The consumer treats it as a tile count, not a flag: groupnorm_sharded_v2.cpp:51 `constexpr uint32_t block_w_last = get_compile_time_arg_val(20);` and :447 `uint32_t block_w_curr = index_g_offset == (per_core_N - block_w_last) ? block_w_last : block_w;`, after which block_w_curr is a loop bound (`for (uint32_t w = 0; w < block_w_curr; ++w)`, lines 452/505/530) and a decrementing bound (`if (index_block_w >= block_w_curr - 1)`, line 482). The identical use appears in the sibling kernel groupnorm.cpp:638/642/667/672/704/737 (fed by the same slip at groupnorm_mcast_program_factory.cpp:195 and groupnorm_no_mcast_program_factory.cpp:206) and in the dataflow kernels reader_mcast_sender_unary_gn.cpp:423, reader_mcast_receiver_unary_gn.cpp:243 and writer_unary_gn_rm_gb.cpp:249 -- every consumer uses it as a width in tiles, none as a boolean. Also note the guarded direction is safe (a false positive is impossible: with block_w_last == 1 the equality can only be satisfied by a group whose true span is 1, which is by construction the last group), so the defect is purely a missed narrowing of the final group.

**Suggested fix.** Declare it as `uint32_t block_wt_last = (per_core_Nt + num_groups_per_core - 1) / num_groups_per_core;` (and do the same at groupnorm_mcast_program_factory.cpp:195 and groupnorm_no_mcast_program_factory.cpp:206 so the three factories stay in sync).

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

items.title: [ttnn/matmul] 5 high-severity defects: 2 bias-CB deadlocks, missing guard, bad overload, wrong interm0 format
items.body:
These are statically audited bugs. The issues have enough detail that you can point claude and ask it to fix them. There is a small chance of false positives.

---

Five high-severity defects in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/matmul/`. Items 1 and 2 hang the op; the remaining three produce a crash, a missing validation, or an under-sized intermediate CB.

**Line references are against `02246470f99`, and every file below was re-checked as byte-identical on `main` @ `007e45f8bfe`, so the line numbers are valid as of filing. If lines have since moved, the quoted code in each entry is the reliable anchor.**

Each item is self-contained — location, triggering configuration, evidence, and a suggested fix — and is independently fixable. Please tick items off as they land rather than closing the issue on the first fix.

CODEOWNERS: @tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce

**Items 1 and 2 are the two halves of one bias-CB credit imbalance** on the batched DRAM-sharded path — the writer re-pushes the fused-bias block once per batch while the compute kernel waits and pops it exactly once, and the CB holds a single block. Read them together; the fix has to reconcile the host CB sizing with both kernels.

Unrelated prior art worth knowing about: #50973 tracked a *different* matmul defect (`reader_bmm_tile_layout_in0_receiver.cpp:80`, mcast receiver readiness credit), fixed by PR #50997. None of the five below is that defect.

---

### 1. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/matmul/device/factory/matmul_multicore_reuse_batched_hs_dram_sharded_program_factory.cpp:191` — cb-credit-imbalance

**Fused-bias CB (c_3) is sized for exactly one block while the in1 writer kernel re-pushes bias once per batch and the compute kernel pops it only once at the very end, so any batched-DRAM-sharded matmul with a bias and batches_per_core > 1 deadlocks.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.linear(a, b, bias=..., program_config=MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastBatchedDRAMShardedProgramConfig(...)) on a device with 12 DRAM banks and B = 24 (the exact shape already exercised by tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/matmul/test_matmul_deepseek.py::test_matmul_batched_dram_sharded_program_cache with batch=24, giving batches_per_core = 2). Batch 0 works. On batch 1 the in1 writer executes cb_in3.reserve_back(in3_block_tiles) (reader_bmm_tile_layout_in1_sender_dram_sharded_height.cpp:109). cb_in3 has exactly in3_block_tiles pages and compute has not popped any of them, so reserve_back blocks forever. The writer therefore never reaches cb_out.wait_front / the output NOC write for batch 1, compute fills the output CB and blocks in reserve_back, and the program hangs (watcher/dispatch timeout).

**Evidence.** Host (this file) line 190-191: `uint32_t in3_block_tiles = per_core_N; uint32_t in3_CB_size = in3_block_tiles * bias_single_tile_size;` -> CB c_3 (lines 262-272) has total_size == one bias block, i.e. num_pages == bias_ntiles exactly. Host line 424 passes `1` as compute compile-time arg 8 (num_blocks_w_dim). bmm_large_block_zm_fused_bias_activation.cpp:497-500 states the contract explicitly: "Reader only pushes bias once when num_blocks_w_dim == 1; the tiles stay in the CB for reuse across bh/batch iterations", and only waits `if ((b == 0 && bh == 0) || num_blocks_w_dim > 1)`. The matching pop is guarded the same way: line 574 `if constexpr (num_blocks_w_dim > 1) bias_cb.pop_front(bias_ntiles);` and lines 619-621 `if constexpr (num_blocks_w_dim == 1) { bias_cb.pop_front(bias_ntiles); }` AFTER the whole `for (b < batch)` loop. The batched writer violates that contract: its bias read at reader_bmm_tile_layout_in1_sender_dram_sharded_height.cpp:107-118 is INSIDE `for (uint32_t batch = 0; batch < num_batches_per_core; ++batch)` (line 76). The non-batched sibling that feeds the same compute kernel does it correctly - reader_bmm_tile_layout_in1_sender_dram_sharded.cpp:158-179 reads and pushes bias exactly once, outside any per-batch loop. Note also that the host passes no bias batch stride, confirming the intent is a single resident bias block.

**Suggested fix.** Hoist the FUSE_BIAS read/push in reader_bmm_tile_layout_in1_sender_dram_sharded_height.cpp out of the per-batch loop (match reader_bmm_tile_layout_in1_sender_dram_sharded.cpp), so exactly one bias block is pushed and the compute kernel's single trailing pop balances it. Alternatively, if per-batch bias re-reads are wanted, size in3_CB_size = batches_per_core * in3_block_tiles * bias_single_tile_size in this file AND make the compute kernel pop bias per batch - but the single-push fix matches the kernel contract and is cheaper.

- [ ] fixed

---

### 2. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/matmul/device/kernels/dataflow/reader_bmm_tile_layout_in1_sender_dram_sharded_height.cpp:109` — cb-credit-imbalance

**The FUSE_BIAS block re-reserves and re-pushes the whole bias block on every batch iteration, but the compute consumer only wait_front's it once and pop_front's it once, and the bias CB holds exactly one block -- so with num_batches_per_core > 1 the second cb_in3.reserve_back() never returns and the op hangs.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.matmul with MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastBatchedDRAMShardedProgramConfig, a fused bias, and a batch B larger than the number of DRAM banks/workers (e.g. B=24 on a 12-bank Wormhole => batches_per_core = 2). Batch 0: reader reserves+pushes in3_block_tiles (= per_core_N) pages; compute wait_front's them but does not pop (num_blocks_w_dim == 1). Batch 1: the reader reaches cb_in3.reserve_back(in3_block_tiles) with 0 free pages in a CB whose total capacity is exactly in3_block_tiles, blocks forever, therefore never reaches cb_out.wait_front/pop_front, and the whole program deadlocks (device hang / watchdog timeout).

**Evidence.** Kernel (lines 76-118), inside `for (uint32_t batch = 0; batch < num_batches_per_core; ++batch)`:
```
#ifdef FUSE_BIAS
        // Read bias for this batch (if fused)
        cb_in3.reserve_back(in3_block_tiles);
        noc.async_read(dram_bank, cb_in3, in3_block_tiles * get_tile_size(cb_id_in3), {.bank_id = dram_bank_id, .addr = in3_tensor_addr}, {.offset_bytes = 0});
        noc.async_read_barrier();
        cb_in3.push_back(in3_block_tiles);
#endif
```
The DRAM source address is `in3_tensor_addr` with no per-batch offset, i.e. the exact same bias data is re-read every batch -- the bias is batch-broadcast, so re-pushing is pure waste even ignoring the deadlock.

Consumer: ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/matmul/device/kernels/compute/bmm_large_block_zm_fused_bias_activation.cpp line 499 `if ((b == 0 && bh == 0) || num_blocks_w_dim > 1) { bias_cb.wait_front(bias_ntiles); ... }`, line 573 `if constexpr (num_blocks_w_dim > 1) { bias_cb.pop_front(bias_ntiles); }`, and lines 617-621 `// For num_blocks_w_dim == 1 the reader pushes bias once and the kernel holds it resident, reusing it across all batch/bh/block iterations without popping. Pop it once here...  if constexpr (num_blocks_w_dim == 1) { bias_cb.pop_front(bias_ntiles); }` -- the comment states the reader's contract explicitly: push once.

Factory: matmul_multicore_reuse_batched_hs_dram_sharded_program_factory.cpp line 146 `uint32_t batches_per_core = (B + num_cores - 1) / num_cores;` (passed as CT arg 6 = num_batches_per_core), lines 190-191 `uint32_t in3_block_tiles = per_core_N; uint32_t in3_CB_size = in3_block_tiles * bias_single_tile_size;` (CB c_3 total size = exactly one bias block, plain local CB with no tensor binding, lines 259-270), and compute CT args 8/9 hardcoded to `1` (lines 415-431) so num_blocks_w_dim == 1. No TT_FATAL anywhere requires batches_per_core == 1 (validate_matmul_batched_dram_sharded_config, matmul_device_operation.cpp lines 1275-1322).

Sibling that does it correctly: reader_writer_bmm_tile_layout_in1.cpp lines 79-101 hoists the identical load OUTSIDE the batch loop -- `// Load the whole per-batch [M, N] bias block once. // It's reused across all of this core's batch iterations (broadcast over batch).` -- and its factory (matmul_multicore_reuse_optimized_program_factory.cpp lines 350-372) likewise passes num_blocks_w_dim = 1 with a possibly >1 batch count.

**Suggested fix.** Hoist the FUSE_BIAS reserve/read/push out of the `for (batch ...)` loop so the bias is loaded and pushed exactly once per kernel invocation, matching the compute kernel's documented contract and the reader_writer_bmm_tile_layout_in1.cpp sibling.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 3. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/matmul/device/factory/matmul_multicore_reuse_mcast_2d_program_factory.cpp:1661` — missing-guard-divergence-from-sibling

**create_program_mcast_in0_in1_descriptor() is missing the TT_FATAL(!(output_is_sharded && B > 1)) guard that its twin create_program_mcast_in0_in1() has, and the descriptor function is the path actually used by ttnn::prim::matmul.**

**How it fails.** ttnn.matmul(a, b, program_config=MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastProgramConfig(fuse_batch=False, ...), memory_config=<BLOCK_SHARDED>) with a batch dim > 1. MatmulDeviceOperation::select_program_factory returns MatmulMultiCoreReuseMcast2DProgramFactory (matmul_device_operation.cpp:2075); that struct declares only create_descriptor()/override_runtime_arguments (no create()), so the mesh adapter dispatches through create_descriptor -> create_program_mcast_in0_in1_descriptor. B = get_batch_size(a_shape_padded) > 1 and output_is_sharded = true, so out_CB_tiles = per_core_M*per_core_N while the compute/writer kernels produce B * per_core_M * per_core_N tiles into a CB that is backed by (and sized to) the output shard buffer and is never drained. The op-level validator does not reject this (validate_matmul_2d only requires BLOCK_SHARDED output and subblock divisibility; fuse_batch is only forced when input A is sharded). The exact combination this guard was added for (#42572/#42580, 'Forge team found a program config that resulted in a hang for matmul') therefore still hangs / silently corrupts on the default path.

**Evidence.** The program twin at lines 1653-1660 has:
    TT_FATAL(
        !(output_is_sharded && B > 1),
        "Block-sharded output is incompatible with batch > 1 (B={}). The output CB is backed by the shard buffer "
        "which only holds per_core_M * per_core_N = {} tiles, but the kernel would produce B * per_core_M * per_core_N "
        "= {} tiles without draining. Use fuse_batch=True.", ...);
    bool do_not_inplace_interm0_out_CB = output_is_sharded && (per_core_M != out_block_h);
The descriptor twin, at line 143, jumps straight from the identical `output_is_sharded` computation (line 123) to
    bool do_not_inplace_interm0_out_CB = output_is_sharded && (per_core_M != out_block_h);
with no TT_FATAL in between. Everything else in the two functions between those points is line-for-line identical (compare lines 96-143 with 1624-1661), which is what makes the omission a copy slip rather than a deliberate difference. `git log -S "Block-sharded output is incompatible with batch"` shows the guard was added by 1389d4aa219 (#42580) as a 9-line, single-hunk fix at a time when the descriptor twin did not yet exist; the later descriptor copy (3934951be50) did not pick it up. The CB sizing the guard protects is duplicated verbatim in the descriptor function at lines 165-171 (`out_CB_tiles = out_shard_tiles` = per_core_M*per_core_N) and the shard binding at lines 1039-1041 / 1087-1089 (`cb_desc.tensor = &out_tensor`).

**Suggested fix.** Copy the TT_FATAL from create_program_mcast_in0_in1 (lines 1653-1660) into create_program_mcast_in0_in1_descriptor immediately before line 143, or better, hoist the check into validate_matmul_2d in matmul_device_operation.cpp so both program paths and compute_output_specs agree.

<sub>CODEOWNERS: `@tenstorrent/metalium-developers-mmfusedreduce`</sub>

- [ ] fixed

---

### 4. `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/matmul/device/matmul_device_operation.cpp:2810` — wrong-argument/empty-container

**The multi-weight ttnn::prim::matmul(std::vector<Tensor>, ...) overload builds MatmulInputs with an EMPTY optional_input_tensors vector, but validate_on_program_cache_miss hard-requires exactly one element (and unconditionally does optional_input_tensors.at(0)), so the whole matmul_batched_weights path throws on every invocation.**

**How it fails.** Any call to ttnn::matmul_batched_weights / ttnn.matmul_batched_weights (matmul.cpp:499 -> ttnn::prim::matmul(input_tensors, optional_output_tensor, attributes)) reaches MatmulDeviceOperation::validate_on_program_cache_miss, which calls validate_matmul_optional_tensors -> TT_FATAL(optional_input_tensors.size() == 1, "Must have exactly 1 optional input tensor, got: 0"). Even if that TT_FATAL were removed, line 2129 `optional_input_tensors.at(0)` would throw std::out_of_range. The op can never run.

**Evidence.** Line 2809-2810: `return ttnn::device_operation::launch<MatmulDeviceOperation>(normalized_attributes, {input_tensors, {}, {optional_output_tensor}});` — the second aggregate member is MatmulInputs::optional_input_tensors (matmul_device_operation_types.hpp:34), initialized from `{}` => size 0. The sibling two-tensor overload 20 lines above does it correctly: line 2788 `{{input_tensor_a, input_tensor_b}, {bias}, {optional_output_tensor}}` (size 1, possibly std::nullopt). Consumers require size 1: line 170-173 `TT_FATAL(optional_input_tensors.size() == 1, ...)` and line 2129 `const auto& optional_bias = optional_input_tensors.at(0);`. **interm0 CB page/total size is computed from output_data_format instead of interm0_data_format, so the intermediate CB is under-sized whenever the two formats differ (fp32_dest_acc_en, or packer L1 acc with a non-fp16b output dtype).**

**How it fails.** sparse_matmul with a DeviceComputeKernelConfig that sets fp32_dest_acc_en=True and a bfloat16 output dtype, with Kt/in0_block_w > 1 (so the compute kernel spills/reloads through cb_intermed0). interm0_data_format becomes Float32 (4096 B/32x32 tile) but interm0_single_tile_size is computed as the bfloat16 tile size (2048 B). Line 599 then creates CB c_5 with total = out_block_tiles*2048 and page_size = 2048. The packer writes 4096-byte Float32 tiles at a 2048-byte page stride: every spilled tile clobbers the next one and the final tile writes ~2048 B past the end of the CB into adjacent L1 (the output CB / other CBs). Result is silently corrupted matmul output, or an L1 overwrite of a neighbouring buffer. The same happens with packer_l1_acc + bfloat8_b output (interm0 = Float16_b 2048 B vs bfloat8_b 1088 B). Nothing catches it: CircularBufferConfig::set_page_size only checks total_size % page_size == 0, which holds because both numbers use the same wrong tile size.

  const auto interm0_single_tile_size = output_tile.get_tile_size(output_data_format);   // <-- should be interm0_data_format
